page: Microsoft Azure E16-8ads_v7 is an x86_64 architecture server belonging to the Eadsv7 family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor operating at 4.5 GHz, configured with 4 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs via Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. The system features 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16.0 GB per core. Local storage is provided via a bundled 945 GB disk, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage. No GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance. The server achieves top-tier results in stress-ng single-core CPU tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Multi-core performance scales to average levels, as shown by stress-ng multi-core and PassMark CPU scores. Memory bandwidth for both cached small blocks and uncached large blocks remains in the average tier. In LLM inference benchmarks, the server demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small models, but exhibits weak prompt processing performance for medium models.

With its high memory density of 16 GB per vCPU and bundled 945 GB local storage, the E16-8ads_v7 offers qualitative resource density advantages for memory-bound workloads. The dedicated CPU allocation and high single-core performance make it suitable for database operations, in-memory caching, and memory-intensive enterprise applications. However, the moderate multi-core scaling suggests it is less optimal for highly parallelized compute-heavy tasks that do not require its substantial memory footprint.
